To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown that the MHC-binding prediction method NetMHCpan can be improved by using a novel pseudo-sequence definition of the binding codel based on the MHC-binding data available.

we developed a novel pseudo-sequence representation for MHC molecules based on structural and sequence information from different MHC molecules and that we showed that this novel representation improves the prediction of MHC class binding peptides.
the MHC class binding cleft can be represented using a pseudo-seq representation, and that the performance of the NetMHC method can be improved using this representation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the improvement of the NetMHC pan-specific method, which can be used to predict the binding affinities of peptides to a large number of MHC class-I alleles.
the development of new methods to accurately predict MHC-peptide binding and to identify potential immunogenic peptides.
the improvement of the NetMHC method for MHC class 1 prediction by a novel representation of MHC molecules using a pseudo-seq representation of the MCH binding cleft environment.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new pseudo-sequence representation is superior to the old one, in particular for non-human MHC class I alleles.
NetMHCpan 2.8 is the best MHC class I predictor available today.
the NetMHC method is the best method to predict MHC-peptide binding for the HLA class I alleles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed new pseudo-sequence representations of MHC class molecules based on the analysis of sequence and structural data from several MHC alleles and have used this information to improve the NetMHC method.
the improved MHC class I binding method is publicly available at www.cbs.dtu.dk/services/NetMHCpan-3.0.
the NetMHCpand method has been improved by a refined definition for the MHC-peptide binding environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the MHC-binding prediction methods should be continuously updated with new information from MHC sequence and structural data, in particular from non-human species, in order to improve the predictive performance of the method.

the MHC-binding prediction methods can be further improved by integrating the knowledge of the MHC sequence polymorphisms and the MHC structure, which are not only important for the MHC molecules but also for the peptide-binding prediction methods.
the MHC-binding methods should be continuously updated to include new MHC sequences and structures to improve the prediction performance of MHC class binding methods.
